open-seo.name: OpenSEO
open-seo.summary: Self-hosted SEO research: keywords, rankings, backlinks and site audits, on your own Cloudflare account and behind Cloudflare Access.
open-seo.tagline: Find search terms, track rankings, and check your site's health

secrets.name: DATAFORSEO_API_KEY
secrets.label: DataForSEO API key
secrets.help: The Base64 credentials DataForSEO sends by email (app.dataforseo.com, API Access, Send by email): the Base64 of your DataForSEO email:password. See docs/DATAFORSEO_API_KEY.md in the OpenSEO repository.

secrets.name: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
secrets.label: OpenRouter API key
secrets.help: Turns on SAM, the in-app SEO agent. Create a key at openrouter.ai/settings/keys; OpenRouter bills the agent's requests. Leave empty to hide SAM.

secrets.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
secrets.label: Google OAuth client secret
secrets.help: For Google Search Console and Google Analytics, with the client ID below. Leave both empty to skip them.

secrets.name: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
secrets.label: Token encryption key
secrets.help: Encrypts the Google tokens OpenSEO stores. Changing it later disconnects Search Console and Analytics until you connect them again.

vars.name: AUTH_MODE
vars.label: Sign-in mode
vars.help: Leave it as cloudflare_access: OpenSEO then signs people in through the Cloudflare Access protection Appflare puts in front of it.

vars.name: TEAM_DOMAIN
vars.label: Cloudflare Access team domain
vars.help: Filled in by Appflare from the app's Cloudflare Access protection: your Zero Trust team's address. OpenSEO checks each sign-in's Access token against it.

vars.name: POLICY_AUD
vars.label: Cloudflare Access audience (AUD) tag
vars.help: Filled in by Appflare: the audience tag of the app's Cloudflare Access application.

vars.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
vars.label: Google OAuth client ID
vars.help: Optional. A Web application client from the Google Cloud Console with the Search Console API (and, for Analytics, the Analytics APIs) enabled. Its authorized redirect URIs are the app's address plus /api/gsc/oauth/callback and /api/ga4/oauth/callback.

vars.name: OPENROUTER_MODEL
vars.label: SAM model
vars.help: Optional. The OpenRouter model id SAM uses, for example openai/gpt-5.6-luna. Leave empty for OpenSEO's default.

vars.name: OPENSEO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED
vars.label: Disable anonymous telemetry
vars.help: Set to 1 to opt out of OpenSEO's anonymized telemetry.

postInstall.content: Open {{appUrl}} and sign in through Cloudflare Access with the email of your Appflare account. Every Appflare user can sign in, and all of them work in one shared workspace with the same projects. The database is already migrated.

{{appUrl}}/api/health lists OpenSEO's configuration checks (DataForSEO, Search Console, SAM) once you are signed in. For Search Console or Analytics, add {{appUrl}}/api/gsc/oauth/callback and {{appUrl}}/api/ga4/oauth/callback as redirect URIs of your Google OAuth client; they change if you give the app a custom domain.

The MCP server at {{appUrl}}/mcp sits behind Cloudflare Access too. MCP clients sign in with Access's Managed OAuth, which you turn on in the Zero Trust dashboard on the app's Access application (Additional settings, OAuth), as upstream's [operations guide](https://github.com/every-app/open-seo/blob/main/docs/SELF_HOSTING_CLOUDFLARE_OPERATIONS.md) describes.

sink.name: Sink
sink.summary: Link shortener with visit analytics: custom slugs, expiring links, QR codes, AI slug suggestions and a realtime globe, all on Cloudflare.
sink.tagline: Create short links and track their visits

secrets.name: NUXT_SITE_TOKEN
secrets.label: Site token
secrets.help: The dashboard's sign-in password and the API key for Sink's API. At least 8 characters; keep it stable, since changing it signs out every browser and API client.

secrets.name: NUXT_CF_API_TOKEN
secrets.label: Analytics API token
secrets.help: A Cloudflare API token with Account Analytics Read on this account, used to read visits through the Analytics Engine SQL API. Without it links still work, but the charts, logs and realtime view stay empty.

vars.name: NUXT_CF_ACCOUNT_ID
vars.label: Cloudflare account ID
vars.help: The account whose Analytics Engine data the dashboard reads: this one. Filled in on every install and update.

vars.name: NUXT_HOME_URL
vars.label: Home page redirect
vars.help: Send visitors of / to this URL instead of Sink's home page.

vars.name: NUXT_NOT_FOUND_REDIRECT
vars.label: Unknown link redirect
vars.help: Send visitors of a short link that does not exist to this URL (always a 302) instead of a 404 page.

vars.name: NUXT_REDIRECT_STATUS_CODE
vars.label: Redirect status
vars.help: The HTTP status short links answer with.

postInstall.content: Open {{appUrl}}/dashboard, sign in with the site token, and open **Links** once: it finishes Sink's storage setup, and creating links fails with "storage not ready" until then.

Visit analytics need the analytics API token. Sink keeps visits in the Analytics Engine dataset `sink`, whose name is shared by the whole account, so install Sink only once per account. A daily job backs up the links to the R2 bucket.

tokenPermissions.reason: Optional: reads visits through the Analytics Engine SQL API for the charts, logs and realtime view.

garrul.name: Garrul
garrul.summary: Self-hosted comments for static sites and blogs: an embeddable widget with threads, reactions and votes, OAuth or anonymous posting behind Turnstile, a moderation queue, and reply emails.
garrul.tagline: Comments and reactions for your website, hosted in your account

secrets.name: TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY
secrets.label: Turnstile site key
secrets.help: Anonymous comments pass a Turnstile check. Create a widget under Turnstile in the Cloudflare dashboard with this app's hostname, then paste its site key here.

secrets.name: TURNSTILE_SECRET
secrets.label: Turnstile secret key
secrets.help: The secret key of the same Turnstile widget.

secrets.name: JWT_SECRET
secrets.label: Sign-in state key
secrets.help: Signs the short-lived state of each OAuth sign-in.

secrets.name: IP_HASH_SECRET
secrets.label: IP hash key
secrets.help: Garrul stores a keyed hash of each commenter's IP, never the IP. Keep it: a new value makes every stored hash unmatchable.

secrets.name: GH_CLIENT_ID
secrets.label: GitHub OAuth client ID
secrets.help: For GitHub sign-in, from github.com/settings/developers, with the callback path /api/v1/auth/github/callback on this app's address. The admin pages need at least one sign-in provider.

secrets.name: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
secrets.label: Google OAuth client ID
secrets.help: For Google sign-in, with the callback path /api/v1/auth/google/callback on this app's address.

secrets.name: DISCORD_CLIENT_ID
secrets.label: Discord OAuth client ID
secrets.help: For Discord sign-in, with the callback path /api/v1/auth/discord/callback on this app's address.

secrets.name: RESEND_API_KEY
secrets.label: Resend API key
secrets.help: Turns on reply notification emails, from resend.com/api-keys. Set the sender address below too.

secrets.name: CF_API_TOKEN
secrets.label: Usage page API token
secrets.help: Turns on the admin usage page: a Cloudflare API token for this account with Account Analytics Read, D1 Read and Workers KV Storage Read.

vars.name: ALLOWED_ORIGINS
vars.label: Sites that embed the comments
vars.help: The origins of the sites that show the widget, comma separated, without a trailing slash, for example https://blog.example.com.

vars.name: ADMIN_EMAILS
vars.label: Admin emails
vars.help: Comma separated. Whoever signs in through OAuth with one of these addresses becomes an admin.

vars.name: PUBLIC_BASE_URL
vars.label: Public URL
vars.help: The app's address, used in comment permalinks and in emails.

vars.name: OAUTH_CALLBACK_BASE
vars.label: OAuth callback base
vars.help: The address the OAuth providers send readers back to; the same as the public URL unless the app sits behind a proxy.

vars.name: EMAIL_FROM
vars.label: Sender address
vars.help: For reply notification emails, on a domain verified in Resend, for example Garrul <comments@example.com>.

vars.name: CF_ACCOUNT_ID
vars.label: Cloudflare account ID
vars.help: The account the usage page reads, with the usage page API token: this one. Filled in on every install and update.

postInstall.content:
Add the widget to a page of a site listed under Sites that embed the comments: ```html
```
Open {{appUrl}}/admin and sign in through an OAuth provider with an address listed under Admin emails. Without a provider set, only anonymous comments work.
Safari and Brave block the sign-in cookie of a `workers.dev` address inside another site, so give the app a subdomain of your site's domain before readers sign in.

secrets.name: JWT_SECRET

vars.name: AI_MODEL

vars.name: AI_FALLBACK_BASE_URL
vars.label: Fallback AI base URL
vars.help: Optional. The base URL of the fallback provider.

vars.name: AI_FALLBACK_API_FORMAT
vars.label: Fallback AI request format
vars.help: Only used when a fallback provider is set.

vars.name: AI_FALLBACK_MODEL
vars.label: Fallback AI model

vars.name: UseBark
vars.label: Bark notifications
vars.help: Push each new code to iOS devices through Bark (https://bark.day.app).

vars.name: barkTokens
vars.label: Bark device tokens
vars.help: The device tokens from the Bark app, in brackets and comma separated, for example [token1, token2]. Only used when Bark notifications are on.

vars.name: barkUrl
vars.label: Bark server URL
vars.help: The Bark server to push through; your own if you run one.

postInstall.content: Open {{appUrl}} right away: while no account exists, the sign-in page lets anyone create the first admin account, so create yours before sharing the address.
Every address of the zone you picked now reaches the app. Use any of them for a sign-up, and the code or link shows up in the dashboard. Promotional mail is kept without calling the AI provider.
AI agents connect to {{appUrl}}/mcp with an API key created in the dashboard (Claude Code, Cursor and other clients that send a header).

mailflare.name: Mailflare
mailflare.summary: A self-hosted email service for your own domains: mailboxes, forwarding rules, and a web inbox, on Email Routing, D1, R2, Queues, and Durable Objects.
mailflare.tagline: Email and shared inboxes for your own domain

secrets.name: CF_TOKEN
secrets.label: Cloudflare API token for Mailflare
secrets.help: A token you create for the app, separate from Appflare's, with the permissions listed below: Zone Read, DNS Edit, Zone Settings Edit, and Email Routing Rules Edit on the zones you will connect, plus the account's Email Sending Edit to send mail. Paste the token secret only, without "Bearer".

vars.name: APP_URL
vars.label: Public URL
vars.help: Optional. The address people open the app at, used in password-reset links and JMAP. Leave it empty to use the address of each request.

postInstall.content: Open {{appUrl}}/setup to check the configuration and create the first admin account. The database is already migrated.
Then add a domain that uses Cloudflare DNS in this account. Mailflare turns on Email Routing for it, sets up the MX and sending records it needs, and routes each mailbox you create to this Worker.
Sending to arbitrary recipients needs Workers Paid with Email Sending turned on for the domain, and the account's Email Sending Edit on CF_TOKEN.

tokenPermissions.reason: Finds the zone of each domain you connect.
Writes the MX and sending records, replacing conflicting MX records after you confirm.
Turns Email Routing on for a connected domain.
Routes each mailbox address, or the catch-all, to the Worker.
Optional: sets the domain up for outbound mail through Email Sending.
